question: An ML engineer is using Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to fine-tune a Llama 3.2 model for text generation. The ML engineer is using an instruction-based fine-tuning method. Which techniques should the ML engineer use to optimize the training?

options.A: Int8 quantization, Low-rank adaptation (LoRA), Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP)
options.B: Float16 precision, LoRA, Single GPU training
options.C: Int8 quantization, Full model fine-tuning, Distributed training

explanation: Int8 quantization reduces model size and memory requirements. Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables efficient fine-tuning with fewer trainable parameters. Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) distributes model training across multiple GPUs, optimizing both speed and resource usage.

question: A company needs to update the model definition of an existing Amazon SageMaker endpoint. Which steps should be followed in order?

options.A: Update the existing model, create a new endpoint configuration, update the endpoint
options.B: Create a new model definition, create a new endpoint configuration, update the endpoint with the new configuration
options.C: Delete the old endpoint, create a new model, create new endpoint configuration, create new endpoint
options.D: Create new endpoint configuration, create a new model, update the existing endpoint

explanation: The correct process is: 1) Create a new model definition with updated settings using CreateModel API, 2) Create a new endpoint configuration referencing the new model, 3) Update the existing endpoint using UpdateEndpoint with the new endpoint configuration. This allows zero-downtime updates.
topic: Section 9: Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) with AWS

question: An airline company deploys ML models to one dozen Amazon SageMaker inference endpoints. The inference endpoints must be able to handle different types of workloads. Match each workload type to the most appropriate inference strategy.

options.A: Real-time inference - For flight departure, arrival, and delay information with low-latency requirements
options.B: Asynchronous inference - For holiday travel promotional deals targeting millions of customers
options.C: Batch transform - For weekly route optimization analysis on historical flight data
options.D: Serverless inference - For occasional forecasting of peak travel periods

explanation: Real-time endpoints provide low-latency synchronous inference. Asynchronous inference handles high-volume requests asynchronously. Batch transform processes large datasets offline. Serverless inference scales to zero for infrequent, unpredictable workloads.
topic: Section 9: Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) with AWS
